# Erik Ninn-Hansen

Erik Ninn-Hansen (1922–2014) was a Danish politician and lawyer who served in several prominent roles in Danish government over a long career, but is perhaps best remembered for being at the center of the "Tamil Case" (Tamilsagen), one of the most significant political scandals in modern Danish history.

## Background and Early Career
- Born on April 4, 1922, in Allerslev, Denmark
- Trained as a lawyer (cand.jur.)
- Joined the Conservative People's Party (Det Konservative Folkeparti)
- Served in the Danish Parliament (Folketinget) from 1953 to 1990

## Political Career
Ninn-Hansen held several ministerial portfolios:
- **Minister of Justice** (1968–1971 under Hilmar Baunsgaard, and again 1982–1989 under Poul Schlüter)
- **Minister of Defence** (1971)
- He also served as Speaker of the Folketing (1989–1990)

He was known as a hardline conservative, particularly on law-and-order issues, and was a significant figure in his party for decades.

## The Tamil Case (Tamilsagen)
This is what Ninn-Hansen is most known for internationally:

- In the late 1980s, as Justice Minister, he was accused of illegally suspending family reunification for Tamil refugees from Sri Lanka, despite their legal right to bring family members to Denmark.
- The case led to the **Schlüter government's resignation in January 1993** after the Tamil Commission (Tamilkommissionen) released its damning report.
- Prime Minister Poul Schlüter's famous denial—"Der er ikke fejet noget ind under gulvtæppet" ("Nothing has been swept under the carpet")—became infamous when the commission found otherwise.

## Impeachment Trial
- Ninn-Hansen became one of very few Danish ministers ever tried before the **Rigsretten** (Court of Impeachment).
- In **1995**, he was convicted of violating the Ministerial Responsibility Act for the illegal halt of Tamil family reunifications.
- He received a **suspended sentence of four months in prison**.
- This made him the first Danish minister convicted by the Court of Impeachment since 1910.

## Later Life and Death
- After his conviction, he largely withdrew from public life.
- He died on May 13, 2014, at the age of 92.

His legacy in Danish politics is mixed: he is remembered both for his long parliamentary service and conservative influence, and as the central figure in a scandal that reshaped Danish political culture and brought down a government.
